title: corydalis micrantha subsp. australis
intro: Corydalis micrantha subsp. australis, commonly known as the small- or dwarfed corydalis, is a species of flowering plant in the poppy family, Papaveraceae. This plant is traditionally used in herbal medicine for its therapeutic properties, which are attributed to its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antioxidant effects. The therapeutic actions of Corydalis micrantha subsp. australis are believed to be due to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids such as protopine and berberine, which have been shown to exhibit sedative and anti-inflammatory properties. Studies have indicated that the bioactive constituents of this plant may contribute to its therapeutic benefits, but further research is needed to fully understand its effects and potential health benefits.
